change.title: feat(agents): stream git worktree-add progress into the chat timeline
change.description:
## Summary

Worktree-mode chat launches previously blocked on `git worktree add` with no visible feedback — the launcher just sat disabled while the checkout ran (tens of seconds on large repos). Now the chat tab opens immediately and a **"Creating a worktree" card renders inside the chat timeline**, streaming git's real stderr output (`Preparing worktree…`, `Updating files: N%`, `HEAD is now at…`) with step indicators and an expandable live log.

## Related Issue

No related issue exists — driven by the bmad spec `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-worktree-create-progress-ux.md`. Searched open + closed PRs for duplicates (worktree progress/loading); none found.

## Type of Change

- [x] feat: new feature

## What Changed

**Backend**
- `src-tauri/src/worktree/mod.rs` — `WorktreeManager::create` takes an optional line callback; new `run_git_streaming` pipes stderr through a `\n`/`\r` splitter (so `--progress`'s in-place `Updating files:` counters arrive line-by-line). `extract_lines` unit-tested.
- `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` — `worktree_create` accepts `progress_id` and emits `acp:worktree_progress` `{ progressId, line }` events (`preparing`/`done`/`error:` sentinels).
- `src-tauri/src/web/worktree_api.rs` — `streamProgress: true` switches `POST /worktree/create` to NDJSON (`preparing` / `progress` / `result` frames). Plain requests keep the old `IpcBody` envelope — old web clients unaffected. WS relay untouched: a first-launch web client has no session subscription, so the request-scoped stream is used instead.

**Renderer**
- `stores/worktree-progress-store.ts` — ephemeral Zustand ops keyed by renderer-generated `progressId` (no cross-talk across launches/windows); collapses consecutive `Updating files:` lines, parses percent, caps at 200 lines.
- `worktree-api.ts` / `web-server-api.ts` — `progressId` + `onProgress` plumbing; chunked-UTF-8 NDJSON reader that tolerates partial lines and malformed frames.
- `acp-store.ts` — `AcpSession.worktreeProgressId` set on the launch placeholder and carried through the placeholder→real-session merge; never persisted.
- `AgentLauncher.tsx` — launch order flips: placeholder + tab open first, then worktree create, then `finalizeChatLaunch` (invariant kept: `startChat` only runs after the worktree exists). Create failure closes the placeholder, restores the launcher, toasts. `handleRestartUpdatedAgent` uses the same flow.
- `WorktreeCreationCard.tsx` + `ChatMessageList.trailingContent` + `AgentChatPanel` + `NewWorktreeModal` — the card renders on every create surface.

## How It Was Tested

- [x] `bun run typecheck` (node + web + test tsconfigs — also run via pre-commit hook)
- [x] `bun run test` — focused suites green (progress store 12, desktop facade + NDJSON 32, AgentLauncher 71); full suite 4966 passed / 2 failed — both are `WorkspaceLayout.test.tsx` timing flakes that pass in isolation and are unrelated to this diff
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets` — clean (remaining warnings are pre-existing `cfg(unix)`-gated dead code on Windows)
- [ ] `cargo test` — test binaries cannot start on this Windows machine (`STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND`, reproduced on unmodified baseline — environment/DLL issue, not this change). CI's ubuntu job covers it.
- [ ] `bun run ci` — repo-wide Biome reports pre-existing diagnostics; changed files are lint-clean
- [ ] Manual verification completed

## CI & Review Gate

- [ ] All CI checks pass
- [ ] CodeRabbit / Claude review comments addressed or resolved
- [ ] No unresolved review findings remain

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional-commit title
- [x] Duplicate-PR search done (none found)
- [x] Tests added/updated (store parsing/collapse, API passthrough, NDJSON reader, launcher flow, Rust line splitter)
- [x] Durable boundary/failure logs added (`log` desktop, `tracing` server, `logFrontendError` renderer)
- [x] No unrelated modifications
- [x] AGENTS.md contributor guidelines followed

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Worktree creation now displays live progress, including preparation, checkout progress, file-copy updates, completion, and errors.
  * Progress is available when creating worktrees from the launcher, chat, and web interface. Logs can be expanded to review Git output.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Failed worktree preparation now cleans up the pending chat tab and restores the launcher, allowing users to retry.

fix: default new terminal and ACP session cwd to main project root

New terminals and ACP sessions were inheriting the last-used cwd (a
worktree path set by a prior ACP chat launch) instead of the main
project root. The root cause was getDefaultCwdForProject returning
worktree.path when activeWorktreeId was set — all new-terminal and
new-session paths funnel through this helper.

Fix: remove the activeWorktreeId branch so it always returns
project.path. Worktree-isolated agent chats already override launchCwd
explicitly (AgentLauncher L995), so worktree-isolation mode is
unaffected. Resumed sessions, chat-row terminals, and the file explorer
use their own cwd sources and are untouched.

feat(agents): stream git worktree-add progress into the chat timeline

Worktree-mode launches previously blocked on `git worktree add` with no
visible feedback — the launcher spinner hid a checkout that can take tens
of seconds on large repos. Now the chat tab opens immediately and a
"Creating a worktree" card renders live git output in the timeline.

- `WorktreeManager::create` gains an optional line callback driven by a
  streaming runner (`--progress`, stderr split on `\n`/`\r` so
  `Updating files:` counters arrive live).
- Desktop emits `acp:worktree_progress` Tauri events; the web
  `POST /worktree/create` route streams NDJSON frames when
  `streamProgress` is set (the WS relay can't be used — the chat session
  doesn't exist yet during launch). Non-streaming callers keep the old
  JSON envelope.
- Renderer progress is keyed by a generated `progressId`, carried on the
  launch placeholder through the session merge, and rendered via
  `ChatMessageList.trailingContent` — ephemeral, never persisted.
- Launch order flips: placeholder + tab first, then worktree create,
  then `finalizeChatLaunch`; `startChat` still runs only after the
  worktree exists. Create failure closes the placeholder and restores
  the launcher with a toast. Same card covers `NewWorktreeModal`.

Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai)

fix(web): emit terminal error frame when streaming worktree create panics

CodeRabbit: a panicked spawn_blocking task dropped the NDJSON channel
without a result frame, forcing clients to infer failure from a truncated
stream. A watcher task now awaits the join handle and sends a result
frame carrying an IoError-mapped IpcBody on panic.

+/** Build an `application/x-ndjson` streaming Response from raw frame objects. */
+function ndjsonResponse(frames: unknown[]): Response {
+  const text = `${frames.map((f) => JSON.stringify(f)).join('\n')}\n`
+  const stream = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
+    start(controller) {
+      controller.enqueue(new TextEncoder().encode(text))
+      controller.close()
+    }
+  })
+  return {
+    ok: true,
+    status: 200,
+    headers: new Headers({ 'content-type': 'application/x-ndjson' }),
+    body: stream,
+    json: async () => {
+      throw new Error('ndjson response has no json() body')
+    }
+  } as unknown as Response
+}

+    expect(op.percent).toBeNull()

+
+  it('appendLine flips preparing → running and records lines', () => {
+    store().begin('p1')

+
+  it('parses Updating files percent into op.percent', () => {

+  })
+
+  it('collapses consecutive Updating files lines into the latest value', () => {
+    store().begin('p1')
+    store().appendLine('p1', 'Preparing worktree')
+    store().appendLine('p1', 'Updating files:  10% (1/10)')
+    store().appendLine('p1', 'Updating files:  90% (9/10)')

+  it('does not collapse non-consecutive Updating files lines', () => {

+    store().appendLine('p1', 'Updating files:  10% (1/10)')
+    store().appendLine('p1', 'unrelated line')
+    store().appendLine('p1', 'Updating files:  50% (5/10)')
+    expect(store().ops.p1.lines).toHaveLength(3)

+    const op = store().ops.p1
+    expect(op.lines).toHaveLength(200)
+    expect(op.dropped).toBe(50)
+    expect(op.lines[0]).toBe('line 50')
+  })
+
+  it('finish marks the op done', () => {
+    store().begin('p1')

+    expect(op.error).toBe('boom')
+  })
+
+  it('handleEvent routes lines and sentinels by progressId', () => {

+  it('handleEvent maps error: sentinel to the error state', () => {

+  it('clear removes the op', () => {

+  })

+

+    expect(mockOnEvent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)

+  })

+/**
+ * Ephemeral progress state for `git worktree add` while a chat launch (or the
+ * New Worktree modal) waits on checkout. Drives the `WorktreeCreationCard`
+ * rendered inside the chat timeline.
+ *
+ * - Desktop: `worktree_create` emits `acp:worktree_progress` events; a single
+ *   `getAcpTransport().onEvent` subscription (`ensureTransportListener`)
+ *   routes payloads into `handleEvent`.
+ * - Web: `POST /worktree/create` with `streamProgress` returns an NDJSON
+ *   stream on the same request; the facade calls `handleEvent` per frame —
+ *   the session-scoped WS relay cannot be used because the chat session does
+ *   not exist yet during launch.
+ *
+ * Ops are keyed by a renderer-generated `progressId`, so concurrent launches
+ * and cross-window events cannot cross-talk: `handleEvent` ignores ids this
+ * client never began. Ops are never persisted — the card lives for the
+ * duration of one create call.
+ */
+
+import type { WorktreeProgressEvent } from '@shared/types/ipc.types'
+import { create } from 'zustand'
+import { getAcpTransport } from '@/lib/acp-transport'
+import { logFrontendError } from '@/lib/log-api'
+import { isTauriContext } from '@/lib/tauri-runtime'
+
+export type WorktreeProgressStatus = 'preparing' | 'running' | 'done' | 'error'
+
+export interface WorktreeOp {
+  id: string
+  branch?: string
+  status: WorktreeProgressStatus
+  /** Log lines shown in the card; capped at `MAX_PROGRESS_LINES`. */
+  lines: string[]
+  /** Latest `Updating files:` percent, or null before checkout starts. */
+  percent: number | null
+  /** Number of oldest lines dropped once `lines` hit the cap. */
+  dropped: number
+  error: string | null
+}
+
+const MAX_PROGRESS_LINES = 200
+const UPDATING_FILES_PREFIX = 'Updating files:'
+const UPDATING_FILES_RE = /Updating files:\s+(\d+)%/
+
+interface WorktreeProgressState {
+  ops: Record<string, WorktreeOp>
+  /** Idempotent transport hookup for the desktop `acp:worktree_progress`
+   * event. Must run before `worktree_create` is invoked so no early git line
+   * is missed. No-op on web (progress arrives on the create response stream). */
+  ensureTransportListener: () => void
+  begin: (id: string, branch?: string) => void
+  appendLine: (id: string, line: string) => void
+  finish: (id: string, error?: string | null) => void
+  handleEvent: (event: WorktreeProgressEvent) => void
+  clear: (id: string) => void
+}
+
+let transportUnlisten: (() => void) | null = null
+
+export const useWorktreeProgressStore = create<WorktreeProgressState>((set, get) => ({
+  ops: {},
+
+  ensureTransportListener: () => {
+    if (!isTauriContext() || transportUnlisten) return
+    transportUnlisten = getAcpTransport().onEvent<WorktreeProgressEvent>(
+      'acp:worktree_progress',
+      (event) => {
+        get().handleEvent(event)
+      }
+    )
+    void logFrontendError({
+      level: 'info',
+      source: 'worktree-progress-store',
+      message: 'acp:worktree_progress listener registered'
+    })
+  },
+
+  begin: (id, branch) =>
+    set((prev) => ({
+      ops: {
+        ...prev.ops,
+        [id]: { id, branch, status: 'preparing', lines: [], percent: null, dropped: 0, error: null }
+      }
+    })),
+
+  appendLine: (id, line) =>
+    set((prev) => {
+      const op = prev.ops[id]
+      if (!op) return prev
+      let lines = op.lines
+      let dropped = op.dropped
+      // `Updating files: N%` is git's in-place counter — collapse consecutive
+      // updates into the latest value instead of flooding the log.
+      if (
+        line.startsWith(UPDATING_FILES_PREFIX) &&
+        lines.length > 0 &&
+        lines[lines.length - 1].startsWith(UPDATING_FILES_PREFIX)
+      ) {
+        lines = [...lines.slice(0, -1), line]
+      } else {
+        lines = [...lines, line]
+        if (lines.length > MAX_PROGRESS_LINES) {
+          const overflow = lines.length - MAX_PROGRESS_LINES
+          lines = lines.slice(overflow)
+          dropped += overflow
+        }
+      }
+      const percent = UPDATING_FILES_RE.exec(line)?.[1]
+      return {
+        ops: {
+          ...prev.ops,
+          [id]: {
+            ...op,
+            lines,
+            dropped,
+            percent: percent != null ? Number(percent) : op.percent,
+            status: op.status === 'preparing' ? 'running' : op.status
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }),
+
+  finish: (id, error) =>
+    set((prev) => {
+      const op = prev.ops[id]
+      if (!op) return prev
+      return {
+        ops: {
+          ...prev.ops,
+          [id]: {
+            ...op,
+            status: error ? 'error' : 'done',
+            error: error ?? op.error
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }),
+
+  handleEvent: (event) => {
+    const op = get().ops[event.progressId]
+    if (!op) return // Unknown id — event belongs to a different client/launch.
+    const { progressId, line } = event
+    if (line === 'preparing') return // `begin` already set the preparing state.
+    if (line === 'done') {
+      get().finish(progressId)
+    } else if (line.startsWith('error:')) {
+      get().appendLine(progressId, line)
+      get().finish(progressId, line.slice('error:'.length).trim())
+    } else {
+      get().appendLine(progressId, line)
+    }
+  },
+
+  clear: (id) =>
+    set((prev) => {
+      if (!(id in prev.ops)) return prev
+      const next = { ...prev.ops }
+      delete next[id]
+      return { ops: next }
+    })
+}))
